issue: Can 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1) be constitutionally applied to a person with any prior felony conviction, or only to those whose predicate offenses show dangerousness, under the Second Amendment as clarified by Bruen and Rahimi?

sides.position: Section 922(g)(1) is constitutional as applied to all felons, based on prior precedent and/or historical analysis, so no as-applied exception is required.
cases: United States v. Hunt, 123 F.4th 697 (4th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Jackson, 110 F.4th 1120 (8th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Duarte, 137 F.4th 743 (9th Cir. 2025) (en banc)
United States v. Dubois, 139 F.4th 887 (11th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Section 922(g)(1) must be applied only to felony predicates that qualify under a Second Amendment dangerousness or historical-analogue test, so courts must determine whether the particular predicate offense supports disarmament (the court favors this predicate-by-predicate approach as more administrable).
cases: United States v. Mancilla, No. 23-10952 (5th Cir. 2025)

this_court: The excerpts do not state the holding, but the reasoning favors the predicate-by-predicate, as-applied side, which is opposed to the categorical rule adopted by the sister circuits listed above.
quote: There is already a robust circuit split on this issue.
cite: United States v. Mancilla, No. 23-10952 (5th Cir. 2025)
